name: Kaya Guava-Sorrel
description: Kaya Guava-Sorrel blends synth-guava sweetness with the tart, spiced character of sorrel (hibiscus sabdariffa variant), producing a distinctly deep-pink soda with a warming spice note. It is the second most popular soda in Tier 1-2 markets and a staple of community gathering spaces.
flavor_profile: Sweet guava front with a jammy body, transitioning into tart spiced sorrel with hints of cinnamon-ginger, moderate fizz, slightly viscous texture
cultural_context: Kaya is a community brand — founded by a Shelf collective that sold corponation licensing rights but maintained a profit-sharing structure with the original neighborhoods. Whether that structure still functions is contested, but the mythology persists. Kaya Guava-Sorrel is served at every community event, memorial, and block coordination meeting in lower-tier residential zones. It carries genuine emotional weight.
story_hooks: The original profit-sharing agreement is about to be dissolved by the corponation that bought Kaya's licensing — and the Shelf collective that founded it is mobilizing to expose the betrayal before the contract renewal date.
A Tier 5 food anthropologist is documenting Kaya's cultural role for a Spire museum exhibit — her presence in Shelf communities is creating friction and suspicion.
Someone is adulterating bulk Kaya shipments to community centers with a compound that suppresses BCI connectivity — subtly, over time — and no one has connected the dots yet.
